cosmetology.hero.title2: The right raw materials are what make them work
cosmetology.hero.description: In a formulation, what matters is not only the function of a single ingredient, but also its impact on the whole system. That's why we look at the choice of raw materials through the lens of application, parameters, and real needs. Are you developing a new formulation, qualifying a supplier, or looking for an alternative? Check out raw materials worth verifying and order a sample for your own tests.

cosmetology.challenges.title: Technologist's challenges
cosmetology.challenges.title1: One change affects the whole system
cosmetology.challenges.description1: Adding an ingredient for a specific function can change viscosity, foaming, stability, or the after-feel on application. That's why every modification needs to be evaluated in the context of the whole formulation, not a single parameter.
cosmetology.challenges.description2: A formula can pass stability tests and still be too heavy, sticky, or hard to apply. The challenge is finding the balance between structure, stability, and the product's expected sensory profile.
cosmetology.challenges.description3: The same INCI name doesn't always mean the same behavior in a formulation. When reformulating, what matters is function, application parameters, and the impact of the change on the whole system - not just the ingredient's name.
cosmetology.challenges.description4: Instead of testing many random options, it's worth narrowing the choice to a few raw materials selected by function, parameters, documentation, and availability. Each of them can then be verified in your own lab.
cosmetology.challenges.callout: Each of these challenges can appear in different types of formulations and at different project stages. Discover five areas where the choice of raw material matters most.
cosmetology.guide.description: Different formulation goals call for different raw material selection criteria. Pick one of the five areas and see which functions, parameters, and raw materials are worth including in further testing.
cosmetology.guide.tip: The choice of raw material and use level should always be verified in the specific formulation based on technical documentation and application testing.
cosmetology.process.title: From formulation need to a lab sample
cosmetology.process.step1.title: Formulation goal
cosmetology.process.step1.description: We start from the function, effect, or constraint that matters for the given project. This lets us pin down which raw material properties actually matter.
cosmetology.process.step2.title: Selection criteria
cosmetology.process.step2.description: We analyze the raw material's function, application properties, and the project's requirements to narrow down the search.
cosmetology.process.step2.highlight: We don't start from a catalog, but from what the formulation needs.
cosmetology.process.step3.title: A specific raw material
cosmetology.process.step3.description: We point you to the raw materials worth considering first, along with the key technical and application information.
cosmetology.process.step3.highlight: Instead of many random options - a few justified directions for further evaluation.
cosmetology.process.step4.title: Lab verification
cosmetology.process.step4.description: We provide documentation and samples of the selected raw materials for testing in your own formulation. Test results confirm the choice or point to the direction for the next iteration.
cosmetology.process.callout: We don't start from a product list. We start from what the formulation needs.
